title: "Schools that win more produce more draftees, strongly in the Power conferences and moderately in the Group of 5"
date: "2026-10-31"
description: "From 2013 to 2025, a school's win percentage tracked its draft rate with a correlation of 0.82 among Power schools and 0.40 in the Group of 5."
followups:
  - "Does recruited talent drive both winning and drafting? Add team recruiting ratings at entry as a common cause."
  - "Do head coaches carry draft production with them when they change schools?"
  - "Season by season, does a winning season come before or after a rise in a school's draft class?"
  - "Do draftees from programs that produce above expectation also last longer in the NFL?"
author:
  - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco"
freeze: auto
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Schools that win more produce more draftees, strongly in the Power conferences and moderately in the Group of 5}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# ---- Packages, data connection and figure defaults -------------------------
# Load the project's functions straight from the checkout with pkgload; the
# repo is never installed (decision 0042). The site build sets CFB2NFL_ROOT,
# a local render finds the checkout from the working directory.
root <- Sys.getenv("CFB2NFL_ROOT")
if (!nzchar(root)) root <- pkgload::pkg_path()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
pkgload::load_all(root, quiet = TRUE)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(
  duckdb::duckdb(),
  file.path(root, "data", "cfb2nfl.duckdb"),
  read_only = TRUE
)
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)
library(duckdb)
library(ggiraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# One interaction style for every girafe figure: a clear hover pop, dimming
# of non-hovered marks, a dark tooltip, and toolbar zoom + PNG download.
set_girafe_defaults(
  opts_hover = opts_hover(
    css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);"
  ),
  opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"),
  opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip(
    css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;"
  ),
  opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5),
  opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"),
  opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
)

# thousands-separated, percent and correlation formatters for inline numbers
fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  formatC(as.numeric(x), big.mark = ",", format = "f", digits = digits)
}
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf("%.*f%%", digits, 100 * x)
r2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
signed <- function(x, digits = 0) paste0(if_else(x >= 0, "+", ""), fmt(x, digits))

# ---- Named players (keyed on athlete id) -----------------------------------
# Key on athlete id, never name: picks has two Josh Allens (Wyoming 2018,
# Kentucky 2019).
subjects <- tibble::tribble(
  ~who            , ~cfb_athlete_id ,
  "Joe Burrow"    , "3915511"       ,
  "Cam Ward"      , "4688380"       ,
  "Josh Allen"    , "3918298"       ,
  "Jordan Travis" , "4360799"
)

# ---- Load the tables -------------------------------------------------------
team_season <- dbReadTable(con, "team_season")
team_draft <- dbReadTable(con, "team_draft")
teams <- dbReadTable(con, "teams")
roster <- dbReadTable(con, "roster")
picks <- dbReadTable(con, "picks")
udfa_ids <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT DISTINCT playerId FROM outcomes WHERE outcome_signed_udfa_d"
)$playerId

tier_order <- c("Power", "Group of 5")
tier_colors <- c("Power" = "#1d4ed8", "Group of 5" = "#f59e0b")
team_colors <- team_color_values(teams)

# Records cover every FBS season from 2010, when the rosters start, so a
# player finishing in 2013 is judged on the seasons they played.
first_record <- 2010L
first_season <- 2013L
last_season <- 2025L
fbs_seasons <- team_season |>
  filter(
    classification == "fbs",
    season >= first_record,
    season <= last_season
  )
# no FBS ties since 2010, so win % is wins / completed games
record <- fbs_seasons |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    fbs_seasons = n(),
    games = sum(games_played),
    wins = sum(wins),
    losses = sum(losses),
    sp = mean(sp_overall, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(win_pct = wins / games)
# a school's tier is the one it held in most FBS seasons
school_tier <- fbs_seasons |>
  count(team, tier_label) |>
  group_by(team) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(team, tier = tier_label)

credited <- team_draft |>
  filter(
    season >= first_season,
    season <= last_season,
    tier_label != "FCS and below"
  )
school <- credited |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    eligible = sum(n_eligible),
    drafted = sum(n_drafted),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(draft_rate = drafted / eligible) |>
  inner_join(record, by = "team") |>
  inner_join(school_tier, by = "team") |>
  mutate(
    tier = factor(tier, levels = tier_order),
    record_label = paste0(wins, "-", losses)
  )

# Tier totals place each player in the tier of their final season, as in
# the previous post; school comparisons use the school's majority tier.
tier_tot <- credited |>
  group_by(tier = factor(tier_label, levels = tier_order)) |>
  summarise(
    eligible = sum(n_eligible),
    drafted = sum(n_drafted),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(draft_rate = drafted / eligible)
tt <- function(t, col) tier_tot[[col]][tier_tot$tier == t]
xfive <- round(tt("Power", "draft_rate") / tt("Group of 5", "draft_rate"))

# Expected draftees: within each tier, a logistic regression turns a win
# percentage into an expected draft rate (kept between 0 and 1), times the
# school's eligible players.
fit_tier <- function(d, x) {
  f <- stats::as.formula(paste("cbind(drafted, eligible - drafted) ~", x))
  lapply(split(d, d$tier), \(g) glm(f, family = binomial, data = g))
}
win_fits <- fit_tier(school, "win_pct")
school <- school |>
  group_by(tier) |>
  mutate(
    expected_rate = predict(
      win_fits[[as.character(first(tier))]],
      newdata = pick(everything()),
      type = "response"
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    expected = expected_rate * eligible,
    above = drafted - expected
  )
curve_at <- function(fits, x, value) {
  vapply(
    fits,
    \(m) unname(predict(m, newdata = setNames(data.frame(value), x), type = "response")),
    numeric(1)
  )
}

# The recurring cast, by id: the school they were credited to and its
# record that season.
star <- function(who) {
  id <- subjects$cfb_athlete_id[subjects$who == who]
  pk <- filter(picks, playerId == id)
  stints <- roster |> filter(playerId == id, season < pk$year)
  last_stop <- slice_max(stints, season, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  first_stop <- slice_min(stints, season, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  rec <- filter(team_season, team == last_stop$team, season == last_stop$season)
  mutate(
    pk,
    last_team = last_stop$team,
    last_season = last_stop$season,
    first_team = first_stop$team,
    n_teams = n_distinct(stints$team),
    season_wins = rec$wins,
    season_losses = rec$losses
  )
}
burrow <- star("Joe Burrow")
ward <- star("Cam Ward")
allen <- star("Josh Allen")
travis <- star("Jordan Travis")
```
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the latest published release, retrieved 2026-10-31. Records
cover FBS seasons 2010 through 2025; players are counted in their final
college season, 2013 through 2025, which covers approximately the draft
classes of 2014 through 2026.*
:::

## 1. Introduction

The [first post](2026-10-31-conferences-landscape.html) found draft picks
concentrated in a short list of schools, and the
[second](2026-10-31-who-produces-draftees.html) found Power-conference
players drafted at five times the Group of 5 rate. This post asks
whether the schools that win, like Joe Burrow's 15-0
LSU of 2019 or Jordan Travis's
13-1 Florida State of
2023, are the schools whose players get drafted.

+ *Expectation: teams that win more produce more draftees.*

## 2. Data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
n_games <- sum(school$games)
n_eligible <- sum(school$eligible)
n_drafted <- sum(school$drafted)
```
:::


### 2.1 Each of 137 FBS schools has a winning percentage and a draft rate

The table defines every term; the 137 FBS schools
(65 Power, 72
Group of 5) played 25,666 FBS-season games from 2010 to 2025 and
had 36,197 eligible players, 3,044 of them
drafted, in final seasons 2013 to 2025.

## 3. Results


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cor_tier <- function(d, x, y = "draft_rate") {
  d |>
    group_by(tier) |>
    group_modify(\(g, k) {
      ct <- cor.test(g[[x]], g[[y]])
      tibble::tibble(
        schools = nrow(g),
        r = unname(ct$estimate),
        lo = ct$conf.int[1],
        hi = ct$conf.int[2]
      )
    }) |>
    ungroup()
}
win_cor <- cor_tier(school, "win_pct")
wc <- function(t, col) win_cor[[col]][win_cor$tier == t]
at60 <- curve_at(win_fits, "win_pct", 0.6)
# each school weighted by its eligible players, a check on small schools
wtd_cor <- school |>
  group_by(tier) |>
  summarise(
    r_wtd = cov.wt(cbind(win_pct, draft_rate), wt = eligible, cor = TRUE)$cor[1, 2],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
wtd <- function(t) wtd_cor$r_wtd[wtd_cor$tier == t]
jmu <- filter(school, team == "James Madison")
```
:::


### 3.1 Within each tier, schools that win more have higher draft rates

*Expectation: teams that win more produce more draftees.* ✅

Win % tracks draft rate closely for Power schools (r = 0.82)
and moderately for the Group of 5 (0.40), where
small schools new to FBS pull the correlation down, such as James Madison
with 78% wins and 0 of 72
eligible players drafted. The tiers sit on separate curves: at 60% wins, a
Power school is expected to see 14.2% of its eligible
players drafted and a Group of 5 school 3.9%.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tip <- function(d) {
  paste0(
    d$team,
    " (",
    d$tier,
    ")\nRecord 2010 to 2025: ",
    d$record_label,
    " (",
    pct(d$win_pct),
    "); average SP+ ",
    fmt(d$sp, 1),
    "\n",
    d$drafted,
    " drafted of ",
    d$eligible,
    " eligible (",
    pct(d$draft_rate),
    "); ",
    fmt(d$expected, 1),
    " expected"
  )
}
school$tip <- tip(school)
p <- ggplot(school, aes(win_pct, draft_rate)) +
  geom_line(
    data = grid,
    aes(y = fit),
    color = "#9ca3af",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(fill = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = team),
    shape = 21,
    size = 4.2,
    color = "white",
    stroke = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~tier, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_team(teams, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Win % (FBS seasons 2010 to 2025)",
    y = "Draft rate",
    title = "Every FBS school's record and draft rate",
    subtitle = "Team colors; each panel has its own vertical scale; hover a dot for the record, SP+ and counts"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 8)
```

### 3.2 Florida and LSU produced 34 and 28 more draftees than their records predict, and Oklahoma State and Kansas State 23 and 22 fewer

The table and bars rank each tier's five schools furthest above and below
their expected draftees: LSU, where Burrow finished after starting at Ohio
State, is second among Power schools, while Alabama's record already
predicts so many draftees that it sits at +15.8. In the
Group of 5, Cincinnati leads, and the three service academies sit among
the four schools furthest under.

```{.r .cell-code}
sc <- function(t, col = "r") sp_cor[[col]][sp_cor$tier == t]

  group_by(tier) |>
  summarise(r_win_sp = cor(win_pct, sp), .groups = "drop")
sp_fits <- fit_tier(school, "sp")
sp_grid <- school |>
  group_by(tier) |>
  reframe(sp = seq(min(sp), max(sp), length.out = 100)) |>
  group_by(tier) |>
  mutate(
    fit = predict(
      sp_fits[[as.character(first(tier))]],
      newdata = pick(everything()),
      type = "response"
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

### 3.3 SP+, which adjusts for opponents, tracks draft rate more closely than win %, most of all in the Group of 5

Replacing win % with SP+ raises the correlation from
0.82 to 0.87 for Power schools and from
0.40 to 0.61 for the Group of
5, as the table and scatter show.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
win_cor |>
  select(tier, schools, r_win = r) |>
  left_join(select(sp_cor, tier, r_sp = r, lo, hi), by = "tier") |>
  left_join(win_sp, by = "tier") |>
  transmute(
    Tier = tier,
    Schools = schools,
    `r, win % with draft rate` = r2(r_win),
    `r, SP+ with draft rate` = r2(r_sp),
    `Plausible range, SP+` = paste(r2(lo), "to", r2(hi)),
    `r, win % with SP+` = r2(r_win_sp)
  ) |>
  kable(
    caption = "Correlations with school draft rate (final seasons 2013 to 2025) of win % and of average SP+ (FBS seasons 2010 to 2025), by tier, and of the two measures with each other."
  )
```

```{.r .cell-code}
window_a <- 2013:2017
window_b <- 2019:2023
win_in <- function(yrs) {
  fbs_seasons |>
    filter(season %in% yrs) |>
    group_by(team) |>
    summarise(win = sum(wins) / sum(games_played), .groups = "drop")
}
draft_in <- function(yrs) {
  credited |>
    filter(season %in% yrs) |>
    group_by(team) |>
    summarise(
      eligible = sum(n_eligible),
      drafted = sum(n_drafted),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(rate = drafted / eligible)
}
windows <- school |>
  filter(tier == "Power") |>
  select(team) |>
  inner_join(win_in(window_a), by = "team") |>
  inner_join(win_in(window_b), by = "team", suffix = c("_a", "_b")) |>
  inner_join(draft_in(window_a), by = "team") |>
  inner_join(draft_in(window_b), by = "team", suffix = c("_a", "_b")) |>
  mutate(change = rate_b - rate_a)
window_cor <- tibble::tribble(
  ~measure                                                   , ~r                                           ,
  "Draft rate 2013 to 2017 with draft rate 2019 to 2023"     , cor(windows$rate_a, windows$rate_b)          ,
  "Win % 2013 to 2017 with win % 2019 to 2023"               , cor(windows$win_a, windows$win_b)            ,
  "Win % 2013 to 2017 with draft rate 2019 to 2023"          , cor(windows$win_a, windows$rate_b)           ,
  "Draft rate 2013 to 2017 with win % 2019 to 2023"          , cor(windows$rate_a, windows$win_b)
)
wr <- window_cor$r
risers <- slice_max(windows, change, n = 2)
fallers <- slice_min(windows, change, n = 2)
movers <- bind_rows(risers, fallers)
```

### 3.4 A Power school's draft rate carries over from one five-year window to the next

Across the 65 Power schools, the draft rate of final seasons
2013 to 2017 correlates 0.68 with that of 2019 to 2023. Early win %
tracks later draft rate about as closely as early draft rate tracks later
win % (0.57 each), so the data cannot say which comes first.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
  transmute(`Earlier window with later window` = measure, r = r2(r)) |>
  kable(

Win % uses FBS seasons in each window; draft rate uses final seasons in it."
  )
```

```{.r .cell-code}
slopes <- windows |>
  mutate(
    team = reorder(team, rate_b),
    tip = paste0(
      team,
      "\n2013 to 2017: ",
      drafted_a,
      " drafted of ",
      eligible_a,
      " (",
      pct(rate_a),
      "), win % ",
      pct(win_a),
      "\n2019 to 2023: ",
      drafted_b,
      " drafted of ",
      eligible_b,
      " (",
      pct(rate_b),
      "), win % ",
      pct(win_b)
    )
  )
p <- ggplot(slopes, aes(y = team)) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = rate_a, xend = rate_b, yend = team),
    color = "#9ca3af",
    linewidth = 1.2,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"))
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(x = rate_a, tooltip = tip, data_id = team),
    size = 2.8,
    color = "#9ca3af"
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(x = rate_b, fill = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = team),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.8,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_fill_team(teams, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Draft rate",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Every Power school's draft rate, 2013 to 2017 to 2019 to 2023",
    subtitle = "Grey dot: earlier window; colored dot: later window; hover for counts and win %"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 13)
girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 11, height_svg = 15)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
exits <- exit_cohort(roster, picks, udfa_ids, reused_ids(roster))
# a transfer-in had an earlier roster season at a school other than the
# one they finished at
transfer_ids <- exits |>
  select(playerId, final_team = team, last_season) |>
  inner_join(distinct(roster, playerId, season, team), by = "playerId") |>
  filter(season < last_season, team != final_team) |>
  distinct(playerId) |>
  pull(playerId)
fbs_exits <- exits |>
  filter(
    eligible,
    # exits carries its own first_season/last_season columns
    last_season >= .env$first_season,
    last_season <= .env$last_season
  ) |>
  left_join(
    select(team_season, team, last_season = season, credit_tier = tier_label),
    by = c("team", "last_season")
  ) |>
  filter(credit_tier %in% tier_order) |>
  mutate(
    transfer_in = playerId %in% transfer_ids,
    credit_tier = factor(credit_tier, levels = tier_order)
  )
# the exit cohort reproduces the credited counts used above
home <- fbs_exits |>
  filter(!transfer_in) |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    eligible_home = n(),
    drafted_home = sum(drafted),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
school <- school |>
  left_join(home, by = "team") |>
  mutate(rate_home = drafted_home / eligible_home)
home_cor <- cor_tier(school, "win_pct", "rate_home")
hc <- function(t) home_cor$r[home_cor$tier == t]
transfer_tier <- fbs_exits |>
  group_by(credit_tier) |>
  summarise(
    eligible = n(),
    eligible_tin = sum(transfer_in),
    drafted_tin = sum(drafted & transfer_in),
    drafted = sum(drafted),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
by_class <- fbs_exits |>
  filter(drafted) |>
  group_by(draft_class, credit_tier) |>
  summarise(
    draftees = n(),
    transfer_ins = sum(transfer_in),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(share = transfer_ins / draftees)
power_class <- filter(by_class, credit_tier == "Power")
p_last <- filter(power_class, draft_class == max(draft_class))
class_tot <- count(by_class, draft_class, wt = transfer_ins, name = "transfer_ins")
class_wide <- by_class |>
  filter(draft_class >= 2021L) |>
  select(draft_class, credit_tier, transfer_ins) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = credit_tier, values_from = transfer_ins) |>
  rename(g5 = `Group of 5`)
p_early_max <- max(power_class$transfer_ins[power_class$draft_class <= 2019L])
cast_tin <- setNames(
  c(burrow$playerId, ward$playerId, travis$playerId, allen$playerId) %in% transfer_ids,
  c("Burrow", "Ward", "Travis", "Allen")
)
```

### 3.5 Leaving out transfer-ins barely changes how closely win % tracks draft rate

Without transfer-ins (Burrow, Cam Ward and Jordan Travis among them, but
not Josh Allen, on Wyoming rosters only), the correlation with win % is
0.82 for Power schools and 0.36 for the
Group of 5. That holds even though Power transfer-in draftees grew from at
most 10 a class through 2019 to 113 of
237 in the class of 2026.

```{.r .cell-code}
p <- ggplot(by_class, aes(draft_class, transfer_ins, fill = credit_tier)) +
  geom_col_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = paste0(
        "Class of ",
        draft_class,
        ", ",
        credit_tier,
        ": ",
        transfer_ins,
        " transfer-ins of ",
        draftees,
        " draftees (",
        pct(share, 0),
        ")"
      ),
      data_id = paste(draft_class, credit_tier)
    ),
    width = 0.75
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = p_last$draft_class - 0.5,
    y = p_last$transfer_ins + 25,
    label = sprintf(
      "Class of %d: %d of %d Power draftees\n(%s) were transfer-ins",
      p_last$draft_class,
      p_last$transfer_ins,
      p_last$draftees,
      pct(p_last$share, 0)
    ),
    hjust = 1,
    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = tier_colors[["Power"]],
    linewidth = 0
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tier_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2014, 2026, 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    x = "Draft class",
    y = "Transfer-in draftees",
    title = "Transfer-in draftees rose with every class from 2021, mostly at Power schools",
    subtitle = "Draftees who finished at a school other than their first college roster; hover a bar for the share"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 7)
```

## 4. Summary

Schools that win more produce more draftees within each tier, closely among
Power schools and moderately in the Group of 5, and the link holds with SP+ in
place of win %, across two separate five-year windows, and without
transfer-ins.


::: {.cell}

## 5. Discussion


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# schools scatter around the fitted curves more than binomial chance
# allows (Pearson dispersion above 1), so expected counts are benchmarks
dispersion <- vapply(
  win_fits,
  \(m) sum(residuals(m, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(m),
  numeric(1)
)
```
:::


::: {.callout-important}
Winning and drafting rise together, but this data cannot say which drives
which.

- Early winning tracks later drafting about as closely as early drafting
  tracks later winning (0.57 each, Power schools).
- Recruited talent may drive both, since the players a school signs shape
  both its record and its draft class; testing that needs recruiting
  ratings at entry.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Schools with similar records can differ widely in draftees.

- Oklahoma State won 65% of its games and had
  25 of 282 eligible players drafted; Florida won
  58% and had 72 of 287.
- The three service academies are among the four Group of 5 schools
  furthest below expectation, likely because their graduates owe military
  service.
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
power_g5 <- c("Cincinnati", "Houston", "UCF", "BYU", "SMU")
power_seasons <- fbs_seasons |>
  filter(team %in% power_g5, tier_label == "Power") |>
  distinct(team)
big12_credit <- credited |>
  filter(
    team %in% c("Cincinnati", "Houston", "UCF"),
    conference == "Big 12"
  ) |>
  distinct(team)
roster_teams <- roster |>
  filter(season %in% 2021:2022) |>
  distinct(season, team) |>
  count(season) |>
  (\(d) setNames(d$n, d$season))()
cincy_big12 <- min(team_season$season[
  team_season$team == "Cincinnati" & team_season$conference == "Big 12"
])
```
:::


A school's tier is the one it held most often, so Cincinnati, Houston, UCF,
BYU and SMU count as Group of 5 despite their Power seasons, and the totals
of the Group of 5 over-producers Cincinnati, Houston and UCF include
seasons after their move to the Big 12. Schools scatter around the fitted
curves more than chance alone would produce, so expected draftees are a
benchmark rather than a forecast. Transfer-ins are detected only through
rosters, which start in 2010 and grow from 227
schools in 2021 to 307 in 2022.
